newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek socialist government wins confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: Greek socialist government wins confidence vote.

text.p: Greece's socialist government won early on Sunday a parliamentary vote of confidence giving Prime Minister Costas Simitis the green light to proceed with reforms in the country's economy and the public sector.
Simitis, whose PASOK party won elections last month, was backed by 161 deputies in the 300-seat parliament while 134 voted against. Five deputies were absent.

The confidence vote came at the end of a three-day debate during which Simitis and his ministers pledged deep spending cuts in the public sector and a strict monetary policy to slash inflation and huge state deficits.
Simitis said his government's top priority was to converge Greece's ailing economy with those of its European Union partners so that Greece could join the European Monetary Union by the year 2000.
But he also pledged to spend billions of dollars to buy new weapons in the next five years to deter what he called territorial ambitions on Greek islands in the Aegean Sea by neighbouring Turkey.
